summary_paragraph: James, a man with a history of COPD, alcohol dependence, and tobacco use, was admitted after presenting with shortness of breath, pleuritic chest pain, and altered mental status due to alcohol intoxication. He was treated for a COPD exacerbation with steroids, azithromycin, and nebulized bronchodilators, and for alcohol withdrawal with diazepam and supportive vitamins. His condition improved over two days, with stable oxygen levels and resolution of withdrawal symptoms. A head CT showed no acute injury, and a chest X-ray revealed no pneumonia. He was discharged home with a plan to complete his medication course and find a primary care provider, expressing motivation to stop drinking and re-engage with stable housing and employment.
